verdict.text: All three findings sent back are fixed and match the code.
The how-to skeleton still holds on the three pages, and the stamp is green.
`loopctl gate stamp` in the worktree: pass on gate pre_commit, gate cli_tests and rows r1, r2, r3, r4 and r6, ending "stamp green: 0e77631e64aa22f893abcb572572c245583ea1b596317b8878e85dc1c757ca90".
Headings on the three pages: title `# How to`, four H2 sections in order, and `### Step N:` numbered from 1 with no gaps.
f2 against embark.hcl: both tasks use `driver = "podman"` with `network_mode = "host"`.
The paragraph no longer names phoenix.
Tempo is the only 4317 holder it names.
f3 against acme.hcl: the job has a `periodic` block, so a forced run makes an `acme/periodic-<id>` child, and the allocation is read from that child.
Step 2 now says to run `just mfa_status` from the repository root (line 48).
Line 46 reads "the podman driver's `network_mode = "host"`, as embark uses".
Lines 64-67 force the run, list the children with `nomad job status acme`, read the allocation from `nomad job status acme/periodic-<id>`, then read the `issue` logs.
Two prose lines in test-acme-job-changes-on-staging.md go past 80 columns: line 77 (120 characters, in Step 3) and line 65 (81 characters, a code comment).
The 80-column wrap rule is not a gate, and line 77 is not part of the f3 fix, so I am not asking for a change.
